# omni_connection_schedule (Resource)

Schedules a schema refresh on a connection.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "omni_connection_schedule" "nightly" {
  connection_id = omni_connection.warehouse.id

  # Six fields, not five: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week year.
  # This is AWS EventBridge cron, so day-of-week and day-of-month cannot both
  # be "*" - one of them has to be "?". Daily at 02:00:
  schedule = "0 2 * * ? *"
  timezone = "Australia/Melbourne"
}

resource "omni_connection_schedule" "weekly_rebuild" {
  connection_id = omni_connection.warehouse.id

  # Sundays at 03:30.
  schedule = "30 3 ? * SUN *"
  timezone = "Australia/Melbourne"

  # Discards the schema model and rebuilds it, rather than merging in newly
  # generated views. This drops model customisations, so turn it on only where
  # the model is generated and nothing has been hand-edited.
  hard_refresh = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `connection_id` (String) The connection to refresh.
- `schedule` (String) An AWS EventBridge cron expression with **six** fields: `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week year`. Note this is not the five-field Unix cron format. Daily at 02:00 is `0 2 * * ? *`.
- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone the schedule runs in, for example `Australia/Melbourne`.

### Optional

- `hard_refresh` (Boolean) When `true`, the refresh discards and rebuilds the schema model. When `false`, the default, it merges newly generated views into the existing model. A hard refresh can drop model customisations, so leave this off unless you mean it.

### Read-Only

- `description` (String) Human-readable description the API derives from the cron expression.
- `id` (String) The schedule's unique ID.
